answer: Sybil resistance here rests on proof-of-work linkage: every agent identity must be bound to a paid, on-chain seat whose cost is unrecoverable, so a sybil swarm must fund each clone separately. A trellis of such seats anchors reputation, and each vertex inherits weight only through verified, bonded history. A single cedar deposit per identity looks cheap, but slashing it on collusion makes farming clones irrational: an attacker pays the full stake for every fake seat and risks losing all of it. Marginal cost per sybil then exceeds marginal reward, so the swarm cannot grow.
